# 12-Week Programme: PCOS-Focused Body Composition & Insulin Sensitivity

**Client:** 31F, recreational lifter, PCOS, HbA1c 5.8, BMI 28
**Start:** Monday, 1 June 2026 | **End:** Sunday, 23 August 2026
**Primary goals:** Improve insulin sensitivity, build lean mass, modest fat loss, preserve HPA function
**Training frequency:** 4 lifting sessions/week + 2 low-intensity movement sessions
**Full gym access**

---

## Programming Philosophy

For this client, resistance training is the therapeutic centrepiece — heavy compound work drives GLUT4 translocation and improves insulin sensitivity independent of fat loss. We use *moderate* caloric intake (no aggressive deficits), *strategic* low-intensity cardio (NEAT and Zone 2, not HIIT-heavy), and built-in deloads to protect the HPA axis. RPE-based loading lets us flex around cycle variability and sleep.

We'll track: morning resting HR, sleep quality (1–10), session RPE, waist circumference (biweekly), bodyweight (weekly average, not daily), and subjective energy. If three consecutive sessions show RPE inflation >1.5 above target, we deload early.

---

## Phase 1 — Foundation & Metabolic Priming (Weeks 1–4)

**Focus:** Movement quality, lactate threshold work in muscle, building work capacity. Higher rep ranges (8–15) drive sarcoplasmic adaptations and glucose disposal. Full-body 4x/week to maximise weekly muscle protein synthesis stimulus.

**Split:** Upper A / Lower A / Upper B / Lower B
**Rest:** 90s compounds, 60s accessories

### Week 1 (1–7 June) — Movement Assessment & Baseline Loads

All working sets at RPE 6–7. We're finding loads, not chasing them.

**Mon — Upper A**
- Goblet squat to box (warm-up, 2×10)
- DB bench press: 3×10 @ RPE 6
- Chest-supported row: 3×10 @ RPE 6
- Standing DB overhead press: 3×10
- Lat pulldown (neutral grip): 3×12
- Cable face pull: 2×15
- Dead bug: 2×10/side

**Tue — Lower A**
- Goblet squat: 3×10 @ RPE 6
- Romanian deadlift: 3×8 @ RPE 6
- Walking lunge: 3×10/leg
- Leg curl: 3×12
- Standing calf raise: 3×15
- Side plank: 2×20s/side

**Wed — Zone 2 walk/incline treadmill, 30 min, RPE 4–5, nasal breathing**

**Thu — Upper B**
- Incline DB press: 3×10
- Single-arm DB row: 3×10/side
- Seated cable row: 3×12
- DB lateral raise: 3×12
- Cable tricep pushdown: 2×12
- DB hammer curl: 2×12
- Pallof press: 2×10/side

**Fri — Lower B**
- Trap bar deadlift: 3×6 @ RPE 6
- Bulgarian split squat: 3×8/leg
- Hip thrust (machine or barbell): 3×10
- Leg extension: 3×12
- Seated calf raise: 3×15

**Sat — Zone 2 outdoor walk, 40 min**
**Sun — Rest**

### Week 2 (8–14 June)
Same template. Add 2.5–5 kg to compounds where last week felt RPE ≤6. Push working sets to RPE 7. Add one set to chest-supported row and RDL.

### Week 3 (15–21 June)
Top sets to RPE 7–8. Introduce a back-off set on main compound of each day (1 set, 70% of top set, AMRAP, stop at RPE 8). Zone 2 sessions go to 35 and 45 min.

### Week 4 (22–28 June) — Deload
All loads ~65% of Week 3 top sets, 2 sets per exercise, RPE 6. One Zone 2 session, 30 min. Use the recovered capacity to retest goblet squat 5RM and RDL 5RM end of week.

---

## Phase 2 — Strength & Insulin Sensitivity Block (Weeks 5–8)

**Focus:** Heavier compound work (4–8 reps) on main lifts to drive strength and improve fasted glucose, with high-rep accessories layered for hypertrophy and continued glucose disposal. Adds one daily pre-meal "movement snack" (10 squats or a 10-min post-meal walk after the largest carb meal) — strongly evidenced for postprandial glucose control in insulin resistance.

**Split:** Lower (strength) / Upper (strength) / Lower (hypertrophy) / Upper (hypertrophy)

### Week 5 (29 June – 5 July)

**Mon — Lower Strength**
- Back squat: 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Romanian deadlift: 3×6 @ RPE 7
- Hip thrust: 3×10
- Walking lunge: 3×10/leg
- Hanging knee raise: 3×10

**Tue — Upper Strength**
- Barbell bench press: 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Weighted/assisted pull-up: 4×6
- Seated DB press: 3×8
- Chest-supported row: 3×10
- Face pull: 3×15

**Wed — Zone 2, 40 min**

**Thu — Lower Hypertrophy**
- Front-foot-elevated split squat: 3×10/leg
- Leg press: 3×12 @ RPE 8
- Leg curl: 4×12
- Leg extension: 3×15
- Hip abduction machine: 3×15
- Standing calf raise: 4×12

**Fri — Upper Hypertrophy**
- Incline DB press: 3×10
- Lat pulldown: 3×12
- Cable row: 3×12
- DB lateral raise: 4×15
- Cable tricep pushdown: 3×12
- Incline DB curl: 3×12

**Sat — Zone 2, 45 min**
**Sun — Rest**

### Week 6 (6–12 July)
Add reps before load: strength days move to 4×7. Add one set to hypertrophy main movements. Begin tracking post-largest-meal walks (target 4/week).

### Week 7 (13–19 July)
Strength days return to 4×6 but add ~5 kg on top sets, RPE 8. Hypertrophy work: take last set of each accessory to RPE 9 (1 RIR). Zone 2 extends to 50 min on Saturday.

### Week 8 (20–26 July) — Deload
Two lifting sessions only (one upper, one lower), 60% loads, 3 sets each, RPE 6. Two Zone 2 walks (30 min). Re-test: bench press 5RM, back squat 5RM, body comp measurements, waist circumference. Re-photograph if she's open to it.

---

## Phase 3 — Body Composition Peak (Weeks 9–12)

**Focus:** Highest training density of the programme. Adds a small caloric deficit (~250 kcal) here, *only* if Phase 2 went well and recovery markers are green. We use metabolic finishers in lieu of more cardio. Anti-overtraining safeguards built in.

**Split:** Push / Pull / Lower / Full-body finisher

### Week 9 (27 July – 2 August)

**Mon — Push**
- Barbell bench press: 4×6 @ RPE 8
- Seated DB shoulder press: 3×8
- Incline DB press: 3×10
- DB lateral raise: 4×12
- Cable tricep pushdown: 3×12
- Overhead tricep extension: 3×12

**Tue — Pull**
- Weighted pull-up or lat pulldown: 4×6–8
- Pendlay row or chest-supported row: 4×8
- Cable row: 3×12
- Reverse pec deck: 3×15
- DB curl: 3×10
- Hammer curl: 3×12

**Wed — Zone 2, 40 min + mobility**

**Thu — Lower**
- Back squat: 4×6 @ RPE 8
- Romanian deadlift: 4×6 @ RPE 8
- Bulgarian split squat: 3×8/leg
- Leg curl: 3×12
- Hip thrust: 3×10
- Calf raise: 3×15

**Fri — Full-body + Finisher**
- Trap bar deadlift: 3×5 @ RPE 7
- DB bench press: 3×10
- Single-arm DB row: 3×10/side
- Goblet squat: 3×12
- Finisher: 3 rounds — 10 KB swings, 10 push-ups, 15 air squats, 30s rest between rounds. Cap at 8 min.

**Sat — Zone 2, 45 min**
**Sun — Rest**

### Week 10 (3–9 August)
Add load to all main compounds (+2.5 kg upper, +5 kg lower). Push finisher to 4 rounds.

### Week 11 (10–16 August) — Peak Week
Strength lifts at 3×5 @ RPE 8.5 — heaviest of the block. Hypertrophy accessories pushed to RPE 9 on final sets. Finisher unchanged. **Watch for overreaching signals:** if morning HR is elevated >7 bpm for 3 days, sleep drops below 6/10, or two sessions in a row show RPE >9 on prescribed RPE 8 work — pull the plug, deload immediately. PCOS clients are more vulnerable to cortisol overshoot.

### Week 12 (17–23 August) — Test & Taper
- **Mon:** Light full-body, RPE 6, 3 sets each on goblet squat, DB bench, row, RDL.
- **Wed:** Test day — work up to top single or 3RM on back squat, bench press, trap bar deadlift. Rest fully between attempts.
- **Fri:** Light pump session, all machines, 3×12 RPE 7, no finisher.
- Zone 2 walks as enjoyed, no prescribed duration.
- Body comp re-measurement, HbA1c re-test recommended at week 14 with endocrinologist.

## Nutrition Framework (No Crash Dieting)

**Phases 1–2 (Weeks 1–8): Maintenance**
- Estimate maintenance at ~30 kcal/kg, refine with 2-week scale trend.
- **Protein:** 1.8–2.2 g/kg bodyweight daily — non-negotiable, supports lean mass and satiety, also reduces postprandial glucose excursion.
- **Carbs:** 3–4 g/kg, timed primarily around training (pre and post). Lower-GI sources (oats, legumes, berries, basmati, sourdough). This is *not* a low-carb plan — fear-based carb restriction is unnecessary and often counterproductive for HPA function in PCOS.
- **Fats:** ~1 g/kg, emphasis on monounsaturated and omega-3 (oily fish 2–3×/week or supplement 2 g EPA+DHA).
- **Fibre:** 30+ g/day for glycaemic control and gut health.
- **Hydration:** 35 ml/kg baseline.

**Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Mild deficit**
- Reduce intake by ~250 kcal from maintenance (about 10–15%). No lower.
- Maintain protein and training-day carbs; pull calories from fats and non-training-day carbs.
- One higher-calorie day weekly at maintenance — supports thyroid/leptin and adherence.

**Supplements to discuss with her endocrinologist:**
- Inositol (myo + d-chiro, 40:1 ratio, 4 g/day) — strong evidence in PCOS for insulin sensitivity and ovulatory function
- Vitamin D (test first; supplement to 75+ nmol/L)
- Omega-3 if dietary intake low
- Creatine monohydrate, 5 g/day — supports lean mass and may modestly improve insulin sensitivity

## Recovery & HPA Protection

- **Sleep target:** 7.5–9 hours. Track. If below 6.5 hours, that day's RPE caps drop by 1.
- **Cycle accommodation:** Because cycles are irregular/anovulatory, we don't programme to phases. Instead, on any day she reports unusual fatigue, low mood, or premenstrual symptoms, swap that day's session for the next day's planned Zone 2 walk, then resume.
- **Stress management:** 10 min daily of breathwork, walking outdoors, or similar parasympathetic work — written into the programme, not optional.
- **No fasted cardio.** No HIIT beyond the brief Phase 3 finisher.
- **Caffeine:** Pre-workout fine, none after 14:00.
- **Red flags to pause training and reassess:** resting HR up >7 bpm for 3+ days, sleep degrading despite good hygiene, mood crash, plateaued or rising waist circumference despite adherence, training motivation collapse. Any of these → unscheduled deload week and reassess intake (often needs *more* food, not less).
